A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Operator Deep Smoothing work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 2012–2021 intraday S&P 500 options, including comparisons with SVI, validation statistics, and evaluations with and without monthly finetuning.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds end-of-day evaluations across four indices and original OpDS interpolation/extrapolation backtests. The accompanying Deep Smoothing baseline values are attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendices B–C retain the same interpolating GNO, nonlocal first layer, subsequent local transformations, graph construction, and fitting, arbitrage, and regularization losses. Expanded explanations and new evaluations do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from intraday S&P 500 options to January 2021 end-of-day SPX, NDX, DJX, and RUT data. Appendix C.5 additionally evaluates January–April 2018 end-of-day SPX surfaces with half their observations withheld under interpolation and extrapolation scenarios.

E2.justification: New Table 5 includes Deep Smoothing from Ackerer et al. as a quantitative comparator in the interpolation/extrapolation backtest; v1 discussed its performance only in prose. Its scores are reproduced from the cited paper, not newly rerun. Existing SVI and OpDS* comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Appendix C.5 introduces 50% input-withholding protocols and separate errors at retained and dropped observations under interpolation and extrapolation. The new index evaluation uses the SPX-trained operator without training on the other indices. Existing splits, training budgets, metrics, and monthly finetuning remain unchanged; exact withholding rules are deferred to cited work.

E4.justification: v2 adds explicit tests of robustness to missing observations and extrapolation in Appendix C.5, plus transfer tests across intraday/end-of-day data and previously unseen indices. Figures 13–16 provide corresponding qualitative cases. The existing finetuning comparison and spatial error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports averaging the new backtest's percentile summaries over 25 repetitions. v1 reports descriptive variation across surfaces but no corresponding repeated backtest. Existing uncertainty displays remain unchanged, and v2 supplies neither seed values nor confidence intervals across repetitions.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports mean relative errors of 0.00272, 0.01057, 0.01629, and 0.00885 for SPX, NDX, DJX, and RUT, alongside spread errors and arbitrage losses. Table 5 adds backtest quantiles, including extrapolation-test medians of 0.9% for OpDS and 1.7% for the sourced DS comparator. Original Tables 1–3 become Tables 2–4 without numerical changes.

T1.justification: The volatility-validation theorem, universality and discretization-invariance statements, and mathematical constructions are retained. Reordering arbitrage conditions, standardizing notation, and moving the Vega equation into Appendix C.3 do not change the theoretical substance. No new proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central operator-smoothing contribution remains. v2 adds an explicit claim of transfer to three indices excluded from training, changes the introduction's broad claim of improving Ackerer et al.'s errors to being highly competitive, and highlights an extrapolation advantage in Section 5.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly attributes the extrapolation advantage to learning from the entire historical dataset. Section 4 interprets cross-index performance as robustness and extends its spread/noise explanation to market-stress spikes. Existing limitations concerning parameter interpretability and dimensionality reduction remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that trained model weights accompany supplementary code, identifies OptionMetrics Ivy DB US and WRDS as the new data source and access route, and reports roughly two minutes on a consumer laptop CPU for 25 backtests. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, and GPU-training details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cont and Vuletic (2023), contrasting its grid-interpolation preprocessing with OpDS. It also reattributes Ackerer et al.'s cited approximately 1% MAPE from January–April 2018 performance to synthetic-data performance. The remaining literature is substantially retained; author-year citation formatting is an editorial change.

P1.justification: v2 introduces nowcasting terminology, rewrites and combines contributions and broader-impact discussion, refines several explanations, and relocates the Vega definition to Appendix C.3. The main section sequence and most methodological and appendix prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 changes document-wide typography and page layout, regroups existing tables and Figures 5–7, and adds Tables 1 and 5 and Figures 13–16. Figures 1–12 retain identical plot content. New dataset labels in example captions include a Figure 10 Dtrain label that conflicts with the stated 2021 test split.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single-index evaluation, v2 provides useful evidence of transfer to unseen indices and explicit input-withholding robustness tests, while improving resource documentation. The gains are limited by the one-month transfer evaluation and incomplete backtest specification: its 2018 dates overlap the stated training window without clarified training independence. The new Figure 10 split-label inconsistency also detracts from clarity. Overall empirical support improves, but the additions do not establish a fully controlled comparison with Deep Smoothing.
